facts.statement: The only known species in the genus Venenosaurus is Venenosaurus dicrocei.
facts.quote: Its type and only species is Venenosaurus dicrocei.

facts.statement: Venenosaurus was a relatively small sauropod similar to the contemporary Cedarosaurus from Utah.
facts.quote: Venenosaurus was a relatively small sauropod, and was similar to Cedarosaurus, another sauropod from the Early Cretaceous of Utah.

facts.statement: Venenosaurus was a small titanosauriform sauropod that measured 12 meters in length and weighed 6 metric tons.
facts.quote: Venenosaurus is a relatively small titanosauriform sauropod, measuring 12 m long and weighing 6 MT.

facts.statement: The genus name Venenosaurus derives from the Latin word for poison, referencing the Poison Strip Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation where it was found.
facts.quote: The genus name comes from the Latin veneno, "poison", in reference to the Poison Strip Member, and the species name honors DiCroce for his discovery of the fossils.

facts.statement: Venenosaurus lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Venenosaurus belongs to the family Brachiosauridae.
Venenosaurus is classified within the class Saurischia.
Venenosaurus possessed a more slender radius compared to other sauropods like Alamosaurus and Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: The radius of Venenosaurus is more slender than the radii of Alamosaurus, Chubutisaurus, Opisthocoelicaudia, and Saltasaurus.

facts.statement: The metacarpals of Venenosaurus were long and slender in structure.
facts.quote: The metacarpals of Venenosaurus are long and slender.

facts.statement: The pelvic structure of Venenosaurus most closely resembles that of Brachiosaurus.
facts.quote: Its hips most closely resemble those of Brachiosaurus.

facts.statement: Venenosaurus featured unusual deep lateral depressions, or fossae, on the outside walls of its tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Venenosaurus had unusual lateral fossae, which looked like deep depressions in the outside walls of the vertebral centra.

facts.statement: Some of the lateral fossae in Venenosaurus vertebrae were divided into two chambers by an internal ridge.
facts.quote: Some fossae are divided into two chambers by a ridge inside the depression.

facts.statement: Venenosaurus is uniquely identified by its flat-tailed vertebrae (amphiplatyan) with neural spines angled toward the front.
facts.quote: The possession of amphiplatyan caudal centra with anteriorly facing neural spines is a unique identifier of this species.

facts.statement: It remains uncertain whether fragmentary fossils from Dalton Wells Quarry belong to Venenosaurus or its close relative Cedarosaurus.
facts.quote: However, it is not certain whether these specimens belong to Venenosaurus or its close relative Cedarosaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Venenosaurus may have possessed a vertebral condition intermediate between primitive and derived titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Venenosaurus may have had a condition intermediate between the two.

rejected.statement: Venenosaurus was a sauropod dinosaur that lived in modern-day Utah during the Early Cretaceous period.
rejected.quote: Venenosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Utah during the Early Cretaceous.
